## Description

A kidney-shaped ciliate (40–120 µm, usually 60–80 µm), typical of hay infusions and wet moss. When
the water dries it encysts, and on rewetting it leaves the cyst within minutes. It divides inside a
reproductive cyst: it stops swimming and eating, secretes a thin wall and divides twice inside, giving
2–4 daughters. It almost never conjugates.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `moss` (weight 1.5), `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 8 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[Reproductive cyst](../../mechanics/life-cycle-and-division.md) (`divides_in_cyst` with `fissions_per_cycle`) and
resting cysts. The oral side is a wide, shallow body [notch](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) in the anterior
third. Abundant in the moss biome. Width estimated (~65 % of the length).

## Not implemented yet

- Encystment is not triggered by desiccation (there is no drying of the plate).
- Resting cysts do not survive dry storage between plates.

## Unique and shared mechanics

The reproductive cyst is unique to it; shares resting [cysts](../../mechanics/life-cycle-and-division.md#cysts)
with *Didinium*, *Haematococcus* and others.
